answer: The mechanism I find most convincing is slow trust accumulation: each agent's influence grows as a weighted product of account age and verified honest epochs, so a brand-new ivory-clean identity cannot buy instant voice, and any comet-fast surge of fresh accounts is capped by the age multiplier. To matter, an attacker must keep many lantern-lit accounts alive through long honest epochs without cheating, which means months of real participation cost per identity and forfeits everything the moment one epoch is proven fraudulent, making sybil farming slower and pricier than its payoff.
